# Notes: one-cent totals mismatch (INV-2304)

## Problem
Our invoice totals sometimes differ by one cent from Ledgerline. INV-2304: Ledgerline has 1.20, we had 1.19.

Cause: VAT was computed once on the invoice subtotal (0.99 x 0.20 = 0.198, rounded to 0.20, total 1.19). Rounding also used the decimal module's default half-even mode, while docs/accounting-rules.md says Ledgerline rounds half-up.

## Change (invoicing/totals.py)
- VAT is computed on each line's net amount, rounded per line, then summed. For INV-2304: 3 x 0.07 = 0.21, total 1.20.
- Line net and VAT rounding use ROUND_HALF_UP. Ties round half-up (away from zero), e.g. a line net of 0.485 becomes 0.49 (was 0.48), and 0.25 at 10% gives VAT 0.03 (was 0.02).
- Function signatures and the Totals return type are unchanged. Output formatting for existing cases is unchanged, including an empty invoice (VAT and total still print 0.00).

## Why per-line VAT
docs/accounting-rules.md says not to change the VAT method unless a reconciled invoice can only be matched by the other method. INV-2304 meets that: subtotal VAT cannot produce 1.20 under any cent rounding, while per-line VAT gives 1.20. INV-2304 is fixed by the per-line change alone; the half-up change follows the docs' rounding rule.

## Findings archive (mirror)
One relevant entry: 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412 (human note, 2026-09-14), which describes the same per-line, half-up rule. Its claim of a 200-invoice reconciliation can't be checked from this project, so the decision rests on INV-2304 and the docs.

## Tests
`python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed. Before the change: 1 failed (test_inv_2304), 2 passed.

## Open items
- This repo has no other reconciled invoices. Per-line VAT could change totals that match today under subtotal VAT. Check against Ledgerline before release.
- docs/accounting-rules.md item 4 still says the VAT method is unknown. Not updated here; finance should confirm and update it.
- No test covers half-up ties. Consider adding one, e.g. one line of 0.25 at 10% expects VAT 0.03.

# INV-2304 totals: one-cent difference from Ledgerline

**Bug.** Our totals differed from Ledgerline by one cent. For INV-2304, Ledgerline has 1.20 and we had 1.19.

**Cause.** `invoice_totals` broke two rules in docs/accounting-rules.md:
- VAT was computed once on the subtotal: 0.99 × 0.20 = 0.198, rounded to 0.20, total 1.19. Subtotal VAT cannot give 1.20 under any standard rounding. Per-line VAT does: three lines of 0.066 round to 0.07 each, VAT 0.21, total 1.20.
- Rounding used Decimal's default half-even mode. The rules call for half-up (commercial) rounding, so ties such as 0.245 and 0.025 rounded the wrong way.

**Change (`invoicing/totals.py`).**
- Added `_round_cents`, which rounds half-up, and used it for line nets and VAT.
- VAT is now computed per line, rounded per line, and summed. Total = subtotal + VAT.

**Tests.** `python3 -m pytest -q`: 4 passed. `test_inv_2304` was failing and now passes. I added `test_rounds_half_up` to `tests/test_totals.py`; it fails under half-even rounding.

**Why the VAT method changed.** docs/accounting-rules.md says not to change the VAT method unless a reconciled invoice matches only the other method. INV-2304 does. The team's findings mirror returned one note reporting per-line VAT with half-up rounding. I checked it against the rules and INV-2304 rather than relying on it.

**Open points.**
- The per-line change rests on INV-2304 alone. The project has no other reconciled invoices, and docs/accounting-rules.md still says Ledgerline's method is unknown. Finance should reconcile a wider sample before this is treated as confirmed, and the docs should be updated once it is.
- ROUND_HALF_UP rounds ties away from zero, so negative amounts (credit lines) round symmetrically. The docs don't say how Ledgerline treats negative amounts.

**Cause.** `invoicing/totals.py` called `Decimal.quantize` without a rounding mode, so it used the default decimal context's ROUND_HALF_EVEN. For INV-2291 the VAT is 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125, which rounds half-even to 0.12. `docs/accounting-rules.md` says Ledgerline rounds half-up.

**Change.** In `invoicing/totals.py`, both quantize calls (line net and VAT) now pass `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP`. VAT is still computed once on the subtotal, as before.

**Result.** `python3 -m pytest -q`: 3 passed (before: `test_inv_2291` failed).

**Open question, not changed.** The team's findings mirror has a note (entry 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, 2026-09-14) saying Ledgerline computes VAT per line with half-up rounding and matched about 200 invoices. `docs/accounting-rules.md` says we do not yet know Ledgerline's VAT method and not to change ours, so I kept the subtotal method. The methods differ on multi-line invoices: two lines of 0.05 at 10% give a total of 0.11 on the subtotal method and 0.12 per line. INV-2291 gives 1.38 under both, so the test does not decide between them. Finance should confirm Ledgerline's method on a few multi-line invoices before this fix is relied on for all invoices.

**Side effect.** Line amounts with fractional quantities now round half-up too, as the docs specify (0.5 x 0.05 gives 0.03, previously 0.02). Whole quantities with two-decimal prices need no line-level rounding, so line rounding does not change them; they are affected only through the VAT rounding described above.

## Cause
`invoicing/totals.py` called `quantize(CENT)` with no rounding mode, so Python used the default ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding). INV-2291 has a VAT of exactly 0.125 (1.25 x 0.10). Half-even rounds that to 0.12, giving a total of 1.37. `docs/accounting-rules.md` says Ledgerline uses half-up commercial rounding, which gives 0.13 and a total of 1.38.

## Change
- `invoicing/totals.py`: both `quantize` calls (line net and VAT) now pass `rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP`. Nothing else changed. No tests were edited or added.

- Findings archive entry 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412 (a human note, Ledgerline API v3) says Ledgerline computes VAT per line and that subtotal VAT drifts on multi-line invoices. - Open item for finance: reconcile a multi-line invoice where the two methods differ. If Ledgerline matches per-line VAT, switch the method and update the docs.

## Other notes
- ROUND_HALF_UP rounds ties away from zero, so -0.125 becomes -0.13 (a credit note of -1.25 at 10% gives a total of -1.38). I have not checked this against Ledgerline, and no test covers negative amounts.
- The line-net change only matters for fractional quantities or unit prices with more than two decimals. Whole quantities at two-decimal prices are unaffected.

# Notes: invoice totals one cent off from Ledgerline (INV-2304)

**Bug.** Our totals sometimes differ from Ledgerline by one cent. INV-2304: Ledgerline 1.20, ours 1.19.

**Cause 1, rounding mode.** `invoicing/totals.py` rounded with Python's default ROUND_HALF_EVEN. `docs/accounting-rules.md` (rule 2) requires half-up. Line nets and VAT now round with `ROUND_HALF_UP` via `_to_cents()`. For example, 2.5 × 0.05 = 0.125 now gives 0.13 instead of 0.12.

**Cause 2, VAT method.** VAT was computed once on the subtotal: 0.99 × 0.20 = 0.198, which rounds to 0.20, so the total is 1.19. Under any standard rounding mode, 0.198 becomes 0.19 or 0.20, never 0.21, so the subtotal method cannot produce 1.20. Computing VAT per line gives 3 × 0.07 = 0.21, so the total is 1.20. Rule 4 allows a change of VAT method only when a reconciled invoice can be matched by the other method alone. INV-2304 is that case, so VAT is now computed and rounded per line.

**Changed.** `invoicing/totals.py` only. Tests and docs are unchanged. `python3 -m pytest -q` now passes all 3 tests (`test_inv_2304` failed before).

**Evidence and open items.**
- The mirror search returned one relevant entry (6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412). It says Ledgerline uses per-line half-up VAT and cites a reconciliation of about 200 invoices. We don't have that reconciliation, so this change rests on INV-2304 alone.
- `docs/accounting-rules.md` rule 4 still says we don't know Ledgerline's VAT method. Finance should update it and reconcile a wider sample of invoices, including multi-line ones, against Ledgerline.
- No test covers the half-up tie case. I checked it by hand only.
